rationale: B wins because it refuses the seductive fake thesis and replaces it with a cleaner, reportable engineering angle. A keeps 'The cloud-only collaboration tool just added offline editing and customer-held keys — a reversal worth examining,' which leans on an orthodoxy the update does not prove; B gives us 'How Notion made a shared editor work with no connection at all,' with a protagonist and proof a reporter can actually ask for. That is the difference between strategy and a clever sentence looking for evidence.
gaps_in_A: 'The cloud-only collaboration tool' and 'a reversal worth examining' are not established by the update; A needs proof of Notion's prior architecture and the alleged reversal before this belongs in the kept set.
'The prevailing belief is that always-online, vendor-managed cloud is the whole point' invents an industry premise, then builds a contrarian angle on it. Nice trap, bad footing.

'Notion bets regulated finance and healthcare buyers will pay for control, not features' overclaims buyer motivation and pricing. The facts say no pricing change for existing Enterprise plans, not that buyers will pay for control over features.
'compliance teams tighten on where data lives' smuggles in a current compliance trend without a supplied regulatory peg. A admits the peg is weak, but the headline still tries to spend it.
gaps_in_B: 'bank and hospital compliance' overnames the healthcare side. The update says healthcare, not hospitals, and gives no healthcare pilot.
'It just shipped the checklist' is punchy but too neat. The update does not prove CMEK, residency, and offline mode satisfy regulated procurement requirements.

'How Notion made a shared editor work with no connection at all' is smart, but it depends on an engineering lead and conflict-resolution details not supplied. Without that source, it is a product blog, not a press angle.

'features that the company says unblocked these pilots' tightens causation slightly beyond the facts. The update ties the features to regulated buyers generally, not specifically to all four bank pilots.
